items.definition:
a customer or a gambler
The pub was full of punters enjoying their drinks.

the act of breathing
The doctor checked the patient's respiration rate.

a frilled collar or a bird species
The Elizabethan costume featured a large ruff around the neck.

the hind part of an animal or person
The butcher prepared a delicious rump roast.

a piece of broken glass, pottery, or similar material
He found a shard of pottery in the ancient ruins.

a type of Jamaican music
Ska music originated in Jamaica in the late 1950s.

a situation or condition in which there is no movement or activity at all
Traffic came to a complete standstill after the accident.

a morpheme added at the end of a word to form a derivative
The suffix '-ing' is often used to form present participles.

a form of gambling, especially on horse races, in which all stakes are divided among the winners
He entered a sweepstake hoping to win a new car.

an involuntary quivering movement; a slight earthquake
The slight tremor of the ground indicated a minor earthquake.

each of three children or animals born at the same birth
The triplets were all dressed in matching outfits.

the watery part of milk that separates from the curds
Whey protein is a popular supplement for athletes.

self-control, determination
It takes a lot of willpower to stick to a diet.

a sharp turn or change of direction
The car made a sudden zig to avoid the obstacle.

a traditional Chinese medicine technique
She tried acupuncture to relieve her back pain.

a heavy steel block on which metal is hammered
The blacksmith hammered the hot metal on the anvil.

an ornament fastened to clothing with a pin
She wore a beautiful silver brooch on her lapel.

decorative flags or streamers; a type of bird
The street was decorated with colorful bunting for the festival.

a raised road or path across water or wet ground
The causeway connected the island to the mainland.

a heavy, broad-bladed knife
The butcher used a large cleaver to cut the meat.

a person or thing used to lure into a trap
The police used a decoy to catch the thief.

the movement of the tide out to sea
We watched the tide ebb from the shore.

a bond, deed, or other document kept in the custody of a third party
The funds were held in escrow until the deal was finalized.

a material consisting of extremely fine glass fibers
The boat was made of fiberglass.

person who solves problems
He's known as the team's fixer, always able to resolve disputes.

a member of certain religious orders of men
The friar dedicated his life to prayer and service.

the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca
Every able-bodied Muslim is expected to perform the Hajj at least once.

progress or movement forward
They are finally making some headway on the project.

a hiding place, especially for criminals
The police raided the gang's secret hideout.

the state or fact of being impossible
Climbing Mount Everest without oxygen was an impossibility for most.

one of several parts of a payment or series
She paid for the car in monthly instalments.

a short sleep; a nap (informal)
I'm going to have a quick kip before dinner.

a person whose behavior or attitude sets them apart from others
He always felt like a misfit in his family.

a native or inhabitant of Mongolia; a member of the nomadic people of Mongolia
The Mongol Empire was one of the largest in history.

black and white
The old photograph was in monochrome.

the state of being nervous
A feeling of nervousness filled the room before the exam.

a powerful antibiotic drug
Penicillin revolutionized medicine.

a plane figure with at least three straight sides and angles
A square is a type of polygon.

light or heat emitted or reflected by something
The bride's face glowed with radiance.

schooler (a person who attends school, especially a young one)
The young schooler proudly showed off her new backpack.

scrimmage (a practice game or fight, especially in American football)
The team held a scrimmage to practice their new offensive plays.

seaboard (a region bordering the sea; a coastline)
Many major cities are located along the eastern seaboard.

shortstop (a fielding position in baseball)
The shortstop made an incredible diving catch to save the game.

smirk (a smug, conceited, or silly smile)
He couldn't help but give a smug smirk after winning the argument.

sociologist (an expert in the study of the development, structure, and functioning of human society)
A sociologist studies how people interact within groups and societies.

stalemate (a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible)
The negotiations reached a stalemate, with neither side willing to compromise.

stringer (a freelance journalist or photographer who contributes to a newspaper or magazine; a line on which fish are strung)
The news agency hired a local stringer to cover events in the remote region.

tarmac (a paved area, especially at an airport, for parking, loading, and unloading aircraft)
The plane taxied slowly across the tarmac towards the runway.

the process of becoming more urban
Rapid urbanization can lead to various social challenges.

a desk or area where someone works
Each employee has their own workstation in the open-plan office.

a substance enclosed under pressure and released as a fine spray
She used an aerosol can of hairspray.

official permission or approval (British spelling)
You need special authorisation to access this area.

bench or bank
The old men sat on the banco in the park.

a biographical film
The new biopic about Queen Elizabeth II is highly anticipated.

a spot or stain
He tried to remove the ink blot from his shirt.

a mobile tanker for fuel or water
The farmer used a water bowser to irrigate his crops.

a secondary product
Heat is a common byproduct of energy production.

politeness; courtesy
Despite their disagreements, they maintained a level of civility.

a close-fitting undergarment
In the 19th century, women often wore a tight corset.

earthenware pot; nonsense
Don't believe that story; it's a load of old crock.

a collection of related sets of information
The researchers analyzed a large dataset of climate information.

a defensive player in ice hockey or lacrosse
The defenseman blocked the shot with his stick.

a genre of electronic dance music
He enjoys listening to dubstep music while working out.

a shelter or trench dug in the ground; a sunken shelter for players in baseball
The baseball players waited in the dugout during the rain delay.
